html:
The Quito Revolution began on 10 August 1809, when leading creoles of Quito removed the Spanish president of the Audiencia and set up a governing junta. Ecuador celebrates the day as the first cry of independence.

Spain itself had been overrun by Napoleon, and the junta claimed to rule in the name of the captive king. Troops from Peru and New Granada crushed it, and on 2 August 1810 royalist soldiers massacred dozens of its leaders held in prison. A second rising was put down in 1812.

The revolution was part of the first wave of the Spanish American wars of independence. Quito was not free until Sucre won the Battle of Pichincha in 1822, and Ecuador became a separate country in 1830.
